claims.claim: JOSS, ReScience, CODECHECK, and ACM artifact policies expose different review objects and warrant different conclusions.
claims.source_locator: JOSS design and review sections; ReScience initiative description; CODECHECK abstract and process; ACM badge definitions
claims.evidence: The sources define repository software review, computational replication reports, independent execution certificates, and differentiated artifact badges respectively.
claims.notes: Claim is deliberately comparative and does not rank effectiveness.

claims.claim: PROV-O, CWLProv, RO-Crate, and Workflow Run RO-Crate provide reusable provenance and research-object semantics but do not themselves decide scientific validity.
claims.evidence: The sources specify representation and packaging of entities, activities, agents, workflows, and run provenance; none claims to adjudicate domain-scientific correctness.
claims.notes: Negative scope statement is limited to what the standards claim to encode.

claims.claim: Claim-centric scholarly representations have substantial prior art in micropublications, nanopublications, and evidence graphs.
claims.evidence: The works explicitly represent claims or assertions with provenance, evidence, argument, or computation.
claims.notes: Used to narrow novelty, not to imply full equivalence.

claims.claim: Global recursive reputation, local trust, and attack-resistant root-relative graph capacity are prior work rather than inventions of this design map.
claims.evidence: EigenTrust defines a global recursive score; Massa and Avesani study local trust; Levien and Aiken define a root-relative flow-based trust metric.
claims.notes: No claim is made that those results transfer directly to scientific review.

claims.claim: The paper proposes a two-layer architecture separating a shared claim/evidence record from plural root-, topic-, capability-, policy-, and time-relative reliance views.
claims.evidence: This is an explicit design choice derived from the evidence packet, not an empirical fact.
claims.notes: Admissible only as proposed design; promotion to recommendation awaits interoperability and comparative evaluation.

claims.claim: Rerenderability, repeatability, reproducibility, independent replication, and scientific validity should not be collapsed into one badge.
claims.source_locator: NASEM terminology discussion; ACM badge categories; manuscript Table 1
claims.evidence: Primary sources support distinguishing repeatability, reproducibility/replicability, availability, functionality, and result reproduction. The exact five-part ladder is the manuscript's normalization.
claims.notes: Manuscript labels the exact arrangement as a design normalization, not universal terminology.

claims.claim: A resource declaration should be multiaxis and include human and agent intelligence as well as compute, storage, access, platform, time, support, cost, and freshness.
claims.evidence: Protocol design judgment motivated by the supplied project requirements and failure analysis.
claims.notes: Requires implementation burden study and independent review.

claims.claim: The two worked cases can be represented without reporting a downselect as equivalent to a full rerun.
claims.evidence: Only narrative design walkthroughs exist in this draft; executable case packets and independent annotation are absent.
claims.notes: Manuscript explicitly calls the cases walkthroughs and marks evidence gates.

claims.claim: Machine checks can establish conformance and discrepancies but not scientific validity.
claims.source_locator: Scope of computational reproduction and independent execution procedures
claims.evidence: Sources distinguish computational checks from broader scientific replication and review; the protocol boundary is a conservative design rule.
claims.notes: Retained as a safety boundary, not a measured finding.

claims.claim: Plural local trust views improve peer-review outcomes relative to global reputation.
claims.source_locator: No scientific-review comparison exists in the supplied packet
claims.evidence: Local trust evidence comes from a recommender setting and cannot establish scientific-review effectiveness.
claims.notes: Excluded from findings and stated only as an open hypothesis.

claims.claim: Polycentric governance is an institutional lens for plural domains, not evidence that plural scientific review works.
claims.source_locator: Ostrom's polycentric-governance framework and manuscript's explicitly limited transfer
claims.evidence: The source establishes multiple decision centers under shared rules; the manuscript explicitly avoids empirical transfer claims.

claims.claim: This design map is the first end-to-end system joining provenance and plural trust governance.
claims.evidence: The primary-source gap audit is incomplete and the supplied closest-work matrix identifies high preemption risk.
claims.notes: Explicitly excluded; do not introduce without a completed novelty audit.

claims.claim: Executable notebooks, continuous analysis, Whole Tale, Galaxy, and ReproZip provide complementary prior-art mechanisms for executable narrative, environment reconstruction, repeated execution, workflow history, and dependency capture, but their cited scopes do not themselves authorize a per-claim scientific-validity conclusion.
claims.source_locator: Jupyter pp. 87-89; continuous-analysis methods and discussion; Whole Tale abstract, architecture, related work, and summary; Galaxy scalability, environment, history, and workflow sections; ReproZip abstract and Sections 1-2
claims.evidence: The sources document the named execution and capture mechanisms. The negative scope statement is restricted to the review conclusions defined in those checked sources and does not assert that later implementations lack additional features.
claims.notes: Narrows novelty and positions these systems as reusable components; no comparative-effectiveness claim.

claims.claim: NISO terminology, COAR Notify, DocMaps, Crossref peer-review registration, Crossmark, NISO version/correction practices, JATS, and DataCite cover complementary terminology, transport, process assertion, registration, status, serialization, and identifier relations, but the checked standards do not natively carry the full MCRP claim-scoped scientific disposition, resource, assessment-mode, transitive-boundary, and local-reliance semantics.
claims.source_locator: Official scopes, event/relation vocabularies, review-object fields, version/update guidance, and explicit non-goals recorded in CLOSEST_WORK_CROSSWALK.md v0.2
claims.evidence: The sources define distinct lifecycle layers and their checked fields. The negative scope statement is limited to those specifications; it does not claim that no implementation can attach richer extension data.
claims.notes: Supports reuse plus explicit lossy-mapping markers. It is not a novelty, completeness, or effectiveness claim.

claims.claim: The attached GW150914-v2 R0 release candidate verifies two registered public strain-file identities, executes a locked laptop-scale filter/correlation path, observes a 5.371 ms intersite lag, rejects a +25 ms adversarial shift against the 10 ms bound, and passes eight machine checks; this supports only bounded computational repeatability and one necessary invariant for the exact registered path.
claims.source_locator: GWOSC v2 event page and DOI metadata; attached case manifests, recorded evidence, and passing conformance suite
claims.evidence: The committed evidence records lag 0.00537109375 s and correlation -0.400196295324; the +25 ms fixture records absolute lag 0.01953125 s and a failed physical-bound decision. The clean replay and seven additional tests pass under the lock-selected environment.
claims.notes: Verification is of the implementation observation only. Human gravitational-wave review, independent custody, archival identity, calibration, original-search reproduction, astrophysical interpretation, replication, and scientific validity remain explicitly unwarranted.

claims.claim: A fresh-context separate executor cloned detached commits ca447e3 and superseding 2c9b4ee, materialized the unchanged dual-platform lock, verified the complete packet index and all ten resource axes, passed eight checks and clean replay, made isolated curve and manifest/lock mutations fail as required, and verified remediation of four record discrepancies; this establishes bounded fresh-checkout execution custody, not independent scientific replication.
claims.source_locator: Attached separate-executor report IR001 and append-only lifecycle event E004
claims.evidence: The report records the exact commit, clean detached checkout, locked versions, 8/8 tests, replayed lag/correlation, 20/20 packet identities, exact ten-axis set, and two isolated adversarial failures. It also records four accepted record discrepancies and nine decomposed independence dimensions.
claims.notes: Implementation observation only. Shared code, inputs, libraries, host/institutional context, and absence of human GW authority remain explicit; human scientific sign-off remains pending.

claims.claim: The attached R0 case now supplies a source-bounded scientific-review dossier that separates literature-supported context, machine observations, local protocol choices, and six determinations reserved for a qualified human; the dossier remains unsigned and supplies review readiness rather than scientific approval.
claims.source_locator: GW150914 discovery Figure 1 caption and observation text; LVC data guide Sections 4 and 10.2; GWOSC quality/injection documentation; detector-characterization Sections 5.2 and 6; attached dossier HD-01 through HD-06
claims.evidence: The dossier explicitly distinguishes supported contextual facts from the exact unvalidated filter, window, correlation convention, 0.30 floor, and boundary judgments. Its human_disposition is null, and the blank form prohibits machine completion of scientific approval.
claims.notes: This verifies existence and bounded structure of the review interface only. Qualified human gravitational-wave sign-off remains pending.
